A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 23 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are available and readable. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original training and evaluation of Chebyshev policies on Mountain Car, Pendulum, and simulated and physical Aero 2 systems in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v5 reports the same original benchmark, simulation, and physical-control experiments, including the results in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The analytical controller, Chebyshev policy parametrization, model components, and training and inference procedures in Sections 2–4 and the appendices are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Mountain Car scenarios, Pendulum task, and simulated and physical Aero 2 control tasks. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including the main ARS/SAC/PPO comparison and the broader RL Baselines3 Zoo comparisons in Appendices C–D.

E3.justification: The main Mountain Car evaluation over 100 starting positions, Pendulum's 50×50 grid, Aero 2 protocol, and appendix training budgets and model configurations are unchanged. The corrected results are not accompanied by a reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: The same optimizer comparisons, MLP architecture tests, polynomial-degree sensitivity study, trajectory analyses, discrete-control checks, and simulation-to-real analyses appear in both versions.

E5.justification: Run counts, seed disclosures, and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged throughout the appendices. Table 4 retains the CH-3-ARS return standard deviation of 0.0987 despite correcting its mean and minimum.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 4 swap the CH-3-ARS Mountain Car mean/minimum returns from 98.74/98.95 to 98.95/98.74. Table 2 updates the mean accordingly; regret changes from 0.65 to 0.44 and its reduction factor from 4.18 to 6.18. Other results and rankings are unchanged. This appears to correct a transposition rather than demonstrate a new training improvement.

T1.justification: Lemma 2.3 replaces ordinary angle characters with standard inner-product brackets, preserving the same constraint and solution. Mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs, including Appendices A–B, are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion increase the claimed Mountain Car regret reduction from 4.18-fold to 6.18-fold. Claims of analytical optimality, universal policy approximation, 277-fold parameter reduction, and applicability to low-dimensional control remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of policy behavior and simulation-to-real performance are retained. The limitations concerning combinatorial basis growth, numerical stability, and uniform approximation versus MLP flexibility are unchanged.

D1.justification: Both PDFs provide the same software versions, initialization and optimization details, hardware, training times, environment implementation information, and code access information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The Hand and Finch reference revises author initials while retaining the same Analytical Mechanics book; this is a bibliographic metadata correction.

P1.justification: Limited editorial changes include correcting 'which as again' to 'which is again,' standardizing inner-product notation, and revising reference initials and the version/date stamp. Section organization and substantive explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands its column heading from 'Pol. π' to 'Policy π.' Figures, table structures, captions, and placement otherwise remain unchanged. Numerical cell corrections are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v3 reports a CH-3-ARS mean below its own minimum in Tables 1 and 4. v5 resolves this inconsistency by swapping those entries and consistently updating Table 2, the regret, and the headline reduction factor. This improves reporting accuracy and internal consistency, while the methods, experimental scope, and supporting analyses remain unchanged.
